note: Overview notes written for this app as a study aid: what each group of ayahs is about. They summarise; they are not the translation.
sections: The Quran sent down in Arabic; Allah tells the best of stories.
Yusuf's dream of eleven stars, the sun and the moon. His father tells him not to tell his brothers, and that Allah will choose him.
The brothers' jealousy: they plot to kill Yusuf or send him away; one says throw him into a well instead.
The brothers persuade their father Ya'qub to send Yusuf out with them; he fears a wolf will eat him.
Yusuf is thrown into the well. The brothers come back weeping with his shirt and false blood; Ya'qub answers with beautiful patience.
Travellers find Yusuf and sell him cheaply. A man in Egypt buys him; Allah establishes him and gives him wisdom and knowledge.
The wife of the man who bought him tries to seduce him; he refuses and seeks refuge in Allah. The shirt torn from the back shows his innocence.
The women of the city gossip; at her banquet they cut their hands at the sight of him. Yusuf prefers prison, and is imprisoned.
In prison: two young men tell Yusuf their dreams. He calls them to worship Allah alone, then interprets the dreams.
The King's dream of seven fat and seven lean cows, and green and dry ears of grain. Yusuf explains it: seven years of plenty, seven of hardship, then relief.
Before leaving prison, Yusuf asks for the women's case to be examined. The women clear him and the minister's wife admits the truth.
The King takes Yusuf into his service; Yusuf is put in charge of the land's storehouses.
Yusuf's brothers come to Egypt for grain and don't recognise him. He tells them to bring their brother from their father next time.
The brothers ask Ya'qub to send their brother with them; he makes them swear by Allah, and tells them to enter by different gates.
Yusuf makes himself known to his brother. The King's cup is found in his brother's bag, and he is kept behind.
The eldest brother stays in Egypt; the others return. Ya'qub grieves for Yusuf but does not lose hope in Allah's mercy.
The brothers return to Yusuf; he makes himself known and forgives them, and sends his shirt to his father.
Ya'qub senses Yusuf's scent; the shirt restores his sight. The brothers ask him to pray for their forgiveness.
The family enters Egypt and bows before Yusuf: his dream comes true. Yusuf's prayer to his Lord.
Lessons from the story: it is news of the unseen; most people won't believe; the Prophet's way; the messengers before; a lesson for people of reason.
